Choose a full checkpoint, not a LoRA.
This studio runs standard SDXL and Stable Diffusion 1.5 checkpoints. LoRAs, FLUX, SD3, refiners, and specialized workflows need additional support. Unknown installed files are labeled for you to check.






FROM DOWNLOAD TO YOUR FIRST IMAGE
Your first local creation.
A practical guide, with the right files and a clear next step.


01 · API ACCESS
Create your Gemini API key.
Open Google AI Studio and create a key for your project. Check its billing and usage limits. Some preview, legacy, regional, or paid models may require additional access.
Open Google AI Studio
02 · CONNECT
Connect for this tab.
Enter your personal API key. It is kept in this tab’s memory and sent directly to Google in request headers. Reloading or disconnecting clears it. Use a private, trusted device.
03 · CHOOSE A MODEL
Refresh the live catalog.
The Gemini browser starts with Google’s documented October 2026 models. Connecting loads every Gemini model returned by the API, across all result pages. Select a model by its exact ID and check its purpose. Gemini runs in Google’s cloud; there is nothing to download.
04 · YOUR FIRST RESULT
Describe what you need.
Choose an image model for artwork, a text model for writing, a speech model for spoken audio, or an embedding model for a numeric vector. Live, video, transcription, and agent models use dedicated interfaces linked from the model picker.

A little help if you get stuck.
I downloaded a model, but it’s not listed.
Check that the complete .safetensors file is in the ComfyUI/models/checkpoints folder used by your running server. A partial download, ZIP, or a file inside a different ComfyUI install won’t appear. Restart ComfyUI, then use Refresh installed in Models. Files configured through extra_model_paths.yaml can appear too.
The web app can’t connect to my server.
Confirm ComfyUI opens at http://127.0.0.1:8188 on your computer. For the simplest setup, run this frontend locally at http://localhost:5173 and allow that exact origin in ComfyUI. If you use this hosted HTTPS page, your browser may block HTTP or local-network access. The local app package in step 4 avoids that issue.
I get an out-of-memory error.
Start with one image, close other GPU-heavy apps, and try Stable Diffusion 1.5 at 512 × 512. GPU-memory suggestions are estimates, not guarantees. Review the ComfyUI hardware guidance for your machine.
My file is a LoRA, FLUX, or another model type.
A LoRA is an add-on to a base model, not a complete image generator. This app currently uses full SDXL or SD 1.5 checkpoints with an included VAE. FLUX, SD3, LCM, Turbo, inpainting, and refiner models require a different workflow or settings. Choose a model from Discover to start with a compatible file.
The first image takes a while.
ComfyUI loads the model into memory for the first job, which can take longer. The studio shows elapsed waiting time. If it stops waiting after five minutes, check ComfyUI’s queue; the job may still finish there.

Set up local 3D generation.
1. Update ComfyUI. Use a current release with the native Hunyuan3D v2 nodes. Follow the official tutorial for dependencies and hardware requirements.
Official ComfyUI 3D guide
2. Download the single-image model. Get the exact 4.93 GB checkpoint below. Review its license on Hugging Face.
Download Hunyuan3D v2 · 4.93 GB
ComfyUI/models/checkpoints/hunyuan3d-dit-v2_fp16.safetensors
3. Restart and connect. Start your server, connect this app, and select Check 3D setup. The app checks the required nodes and detects the checkpoint. Hardware needs exceed those of many 2D models; see the official guide.
4. Choose a mode. Image to 3D needs a PNG, JPEG, or WebP with a single centered object against a clean background. Text to 3D also needs a full SDXL or SD 1.5 checkpoint to generate the input image first.
5. Generate and inspect. Rotate and zoom the mesh, then download the GLB. This workflow produces geometry without textures. Results and download links last for this session and depend on your local server.
